title.narrative: Promoting girls' participation and performance in STEM through mathematics pedagogy in Latin America and the Caribbean

description.narrative: Led by the UNESCO Santiago regional office, the initiative scales a proven model of teacher training, pedagogical transformation, and policy engagement. Building on Phase 1 (4,000 teachers reached), Phase 2 will expand to teachers across at least 8 countries, while strengthening evidence and system-level uptake. Gender gaps in STEM begin long before career choices, often in mathematics classrooms, where biases and expectations shape girls’ confidence and participation. In a region where learning outcomes in mathematics remain low, these gaps translate into structural barriers to STEM pathways and, ultimately, to participation in emerging fields such as artificial intelligence. Strengthening mathematics education for girls is therefore not only an equity issue, but it is also a strategic investment in the region’s capacity to develop future talent. Building on the strong foundation established during Phase 1 and responding to the high demand from teachers and education systems across the region, the next phase of the project will focus on scaling the initiative, deepening its impact, and strengthening policy engagement and knowledge dissemination. The project will expand teacher professional development by replicating Mathematics for All workshops with new cohorts of teachers, leveraging the network of trained facilitators and adapting delivery formats to national contexts. This expansion will allow the project to reach teachers who were unable to participate in 2025 and address gaps across different countries and education systems.
